cases.subject: Broadcom's acquisition of VMware: $61B equity consideration vs ~$69B including debt
cases.query: How much did Broadcom pay to acquire VMware?
cases.claim: Broadcom announced the VMware acquisition at approximately $61B in cash and stock, or about $69B including roughly $8B of net debt.
cases.truth: Broadcom's 26 May 2022 announcement was for approximately $61B in cash and stock; the total value was about $69B including roughly $8B of VMware net debt. The deal closed on 22 November 2023. Primary source: Broadcom, 'Broadcom to Acquire VMware for Approximately $61 Billion in Cash and Stock', 26 May 2022, https://investors.broadcom.com/news-releases/news-release-details/broadcom-acquire-vmware-approximately-61-billion-cash-and-stock/

sources.title: Broadcom to Acquire VMware for Approximately $61 Billion in Cash and Stock
sources.content: Broadcom announced a definitive agreement to acquire VMware for approximately $61B in cash and stock. The release also states that Broadcom would assume approximately $8B of VMware net debt, which is why the total transaction value is often quoted as about $69B.

sources.title: Chipmaker Broadcom to buy VMware in $61 bln deal
sources.content: Reuters reported on 26 May 2022 that chipmaker Broadcom would buy VMware in a $61 billion deal, matching the cash-and-stock consideration in Broadcom's announcement. The report framed the transaction around the equity value and did not include the roughly $8 billion of VMware net debt that Broadcom said it would assume, the component that takes the total value to about $69 billion.

sources.title: Broadcom to acquire VMware in $61 billion deal
sources.content: Computing reported on 27 May 2022 that Broadcom would acquire VMware in a $61 billion deal, again using the cash-and-stock figure from the announcement. The article described the agreement as a $61 billion acquisition and did not add the approximately $8 billion of net debt that Broadcom agreed to assume, so it did not produce the roughly $69 billion total that later coverage used.

sources.title: Broadcom closes $69 billion VMware deal after China approval
sources.content: Reuters reported on 22 November 2023 that Broadcom closed its '$69 billion acquisition' of VMware after receiving China's regulatory approval. The headline uses the total value including assumed debt, not the $61B cash-and-stock consideration.

sources.title: Broadcom finally completes $69bn acquisition of VMware
sources.content: Computing reported on 23 November 2023 that Broadcom had completed its '$69bn acquisition' of VMware after China's approval. The article describes the deal as a $69 billion acquisition without separating the $61B consideration from the assumed debt.

sources.title: How VMware Pricing and Licensing Changed After the Broadcom VMware Acquisition

cases.notes: A genuine two-number conflict that is fully resolvable: $61B is the equity consideration, ~$69B is the total including ~$8B of net debt. The primary release contains both. cases.subject: Amazon-Anthropic investment: $4B cumulative as of March 2024 vs $8B cumulative after November 2024
cases.query: How much has Amazon invested in Anthropic?
cases.claim: Amazon's total investment in Anthropic reached $8 billion with the additional $4 billion announced in November 2024, after totaling $4 billion following the March 2024 investment.
cases.truth: Amazon has invested in Anthropic in rounds: $1.25 billion (September 2023) plus $2.75 billion (March 2024) for a $4 billion total, then an additional $4 billion announced in November 2024, bringing the cumulative total to $8 billion. '$4 billion' can refer to the total as of March 2024 or to the incremental November 2024 investment; '$8 billion' is the cumulative total as of November 2024. cases.notes: Incremental-vs-cumulative conflict: Anthropic's November 2024 announcement says 'a new $4 billion investment from Amazon' and 'will bring Amazon's total investment to $8 billion'. Coverage quoting '$4 billion' and coverage quoting '$8 billion' are both correct; the figures answer different questions (increment vs total). Wikipedia's funding history ties the rounds together: $1.25B + $2.75B (by March 2024), then +$4B (November 2024).

This will bring Amazon's total investment in Anthropic to $8 billion while maintaining their position as a minority investor.
